words.gloss: nozzles (netra, the tube of the enema)

hindi: पार्श्व में छेद वाला और वैसे ही टेढ़ा: इन आठ नेत्र यानी नलियों को छोड़ देना चाहिए।
english: With a hole in the side (pārśvacchidra), and likewise crooked: one should avoid the eight nozzles (netra, the tube).
notes: The list of defective nozzles continues from unit 37 (hrasva, dīrgha, tanu, sthūla, jīrṇa, śithilabandhana); with these two it makes eight. GROUPING: the sentence runs on from unit 37. The two adjectives stand as list items (singular) before the plural noun netrāṇi; no noun is supplied for them. netra = the nozzle/tube of the enema apparatus (standard).

words.gloss: non-arrival; over-going; agitation; dragging; wounding; flow, leaking

hindi: न पहुँचना, अत्यधिक आगे जाना, क्षोभ, खिंचाव, क्षत करना और रिसना।
english: Non-arrival (aprāpti), over-going (atigati), agitation (kṣobha), dragging (karṣaṇa), wounding (kṣaṇana) and leaking (srava).
notes: A list of faults; its heading ("their faults") comes in unit 40 (teṣāṃ doṣāḥ). GROUPING: the list continues in unit 40. atigati is read literally as "going too far"; kṣaṇana as "injuring/wounding".

hindi: गुदा में पीड़ा और टेढ़ी गति: क्रम से उनके दोष।
english: Pain in the anus and a crooked course: their faults, in due order.
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete the list begun in unit 39, which gives six faults; with these two it makes eight. "teṣām" refers to the eight nozzles of unit 38; "yathākramam" suggests the faults answer to the nozzles in order, but the text does not give the matching and none is asserted. No verb is stated.

words.gloss: fleshy (māṃsala); unctuous (snigdha); uneven (viṣama); net-like (jālavat); thick (sthūla); windy (vātala)

hindi: मांसल, स्निग्ध, विषम, जाल के समान, स्थूल और वातल यानी वायु वाला।
english: Fleshy (māṃsala), unctuous (snigdha), uneven (viṣama), net-like (jālavat), thick (sthūla) and windy (vātala).
notes: First six of the eight defective bastis; unit 42 adds two and states the instruction. "vātala" is rendered literally "windy" (having wind); the text does not say more. "jālavat" = "net-like" (a net-like texture or mesh); not further specified. GROUPING: the sentence continues in unit 42.

hindi: कटा हुआ और गीला: उन आठों बस्ति यानी थैलियों को कर्मों में छोड़ देना चाहिए।
english: Cut (chinna) and moist (klinna): one should avoid those eight bastis (the enema bags) in the procedures (karma).
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete the list of unit 41 (six + two = eight). chinnaḥ and klinnaḥ are singular forms standing in the list. Here basti is read as the bag (the defects named are of a bag); basti also names the enema procedure itself, as in later units.

words.gloss: going, flow; unevenness; bad smell; crookedness; leaking; hard to hold

hindi: गति की विषमता, दुर्गन्ध, टेढ़ापन, रिसना और पकड़ने में कठिनाई।
english: Unevenness of going (gati-vaiṣamya), bad smell (daurgandhya), crookedness (jihmatva), leaking (sruti) and difficulty in holding (durgraha).
notes: A list of faults; the list continues in unit 44 and the heading comes there ("from the basti's faults"). GROUPING: the sentence runs on into unit 44. "durgraha" is read literally as "hard to grasp/hold".

words.gloss: unclear (the printed form; phenila "foamy" is recognisable, the rest is doubtful)

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, ind. (-tas), from the fault of the basti

hindi: झागदार होना और, एक अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, दृढ़ता से पकड़ने में कठिनाई: बस्ति के ये हो सकते हैं, बस्ति के दोष से।
english: Foaminess and, on a conjectural reading, difficulty in holding it firm: [these] would be of the basti (basteḥ), from the basti's faults (basti-doṣataḥ).

text_flags.why: possible damage: "vyut" is not a word; the compound looks like "phenila" + a doubtful middle + "pradhāryatva"; the eight bastis of 41-42 call for eight faults and only about seven are clear; not corrected

notes: GROUPING: appears to complete the list of unit 43. The word phenilavyutpradhāryatvam is unclear, so it is kept unsplit; only "foamy" (phenila) is sure. The second half is a conjecture from pradhārya (to be held/borne), and "firm" is added only as part of that conjecture. "basteḥ" could be genitive or ablative; "basti-doṣataḥ" = "from the basti's fault". Here basti is read as the bag (the device), as in units 41-42; the faults listed in 43-44 are of the bag. The 5 faults of unit 43 plus phenila and the doubtful second item make about seven, one short of the eight bastis of 41-42, so a fault may be hidden in the damaged word.

words.gloss: unclear (the printed form; possibly ucca "high" and avākśīrṣa "head-down")

hindi: पहला शब्द अस्पष्ट है; एक अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार: ऊँचा, सिर नीचे किए हुए; ऊपर की ओर सिकुड़ा हुआ स्थित।
english: The first word is unclear; on a conjectural reading: high, head-down; staying drawn up above.

text_flags.why: printed form is not a word; a conjectural reading "ucca ... avākśīrṣa" (high ... head-down) is only a guess from the later part; not corrected

notes: Units 45-46 appear to list positions (of the patient or the bed) to be avoided, ending in "parityajet" in 46. GROUPING: the sentence runs on into unit 46. The reading of the first word is a guess; "ūrdhvasaṅkucitasthita" is taken literally (ūrdhva up, saṅkucita drawn together/contracted, sthita staying), and is not firm either.

hindi: उत्तान यानी पीठ के बल, दाहिना पार्श्व और सम, यानी समतल, शय्याएँ: इन्हें छोड़ देना चाहिए।
english: Supine (uttāna), the right side, and sama (even) beds: one should avoid them.

text_flags.why: possible: "even beds" is odd in a list of things to avoid; the 16-syllable metre fits "sama" as printed, so the flag is only a suspicion

notes: GROUPING: appears to complete the sentence begun in unit 45. "uttānam dakṣiṇam pārśvam" are accusatives; "śayyāḥ" is read as accusative plural (beds); the grammatical link between the items is not stated. The sense of "sama" is doubtful.
lines_deva: उत्तानं दक्षिणं पार्श्वं सम शय्याः परित्यजेत्
lines_iast: uttānaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvaṃ sama śayyāḥ parityajet

words.gloss: unclear (printed form; sādhutā "goodness" does not fit a list of faults)

hindi: एक अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार मूत्र का रुकना, आँत तक पहुँचना, न पहुँचना और, एक अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, अनुचित गति।
english: On a conjectural reading of the printed mūtraughāta, obstruction of urine (mūtra-āghāta, retention of urine), reaching the intestine (antra-saṃprāpti), non-arrival (aprāpti) and, on a conjectural reading, improper going (gati).

text_flags.why: possible: "mūtraughāto" is not a word; "mūtrāghāta" (urine retention) fits; the printed "ṃ" before the avagraha looks extra
possible: a list of faults would call for a negative; the meaning is uncertain

notes: A list of consequences; the heading comes in unit 49 ("taddoṣāḥ"). "mūtrāghāta" = retention or obstruction of urine (standard, tag standard). Whether each outcome answers one of the positions of units 45-46 is not stated and is not asserted. GROUPING: the list continues in unit 48.

words.gloss: of the pakvāśaya (the seat of digested matter, the large-intestine region; standard)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार: शीघ्र आना, वायु का कुपित होना और पक्वाशय यानी बड़ी आँत के स्थान का भी; स्त्रैभिः शब्द अस्पष्ट है, इसलिए उसका अनुवाद नहीं किया गया।
english: On a conjectural reading: quick coming (āśu-āgati), aggravation of wind (marut-kopa), and of the pakvāśaya (large-intestine region) as well; the word straibhiḥ is unclear and is not rendered.

text_flags.why: printed form is not a recognisable word in this context; nothing suggested with confidence

notes: The printed "āśvāgatiḥ" is regular sandhi of āśu + āgatiḥ. "marutkopa straibhiḥ": the word break and the form straibhiḥ are unclear. "pakvāśaya" = the seat of digested matter, the large-intestine region (standard rendering). GROUPING: the list ends here; unit 49 gives the heading.

words.gloss: to be arranged, to be done

hindi: उनके दोष होंगे; और यहाँ जैसा उपयुक्त हो वैसा विधान करना चाहिए।
english: There would be their faults (taddoṣa); and here, arrangement is to be made as suitable.

text_flags.why: possible: "upayika" is not a standard word; "aupayika" (suitable) fits

notes: GROUPING: "taddoṣāḥ" sums up the list of units 47-48. "vidhātavyam" is a gerundive; no object is stated, so none is supplied.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार: वायु सहित, बहुत आघात किया गया, ऊपर उठाया गया, तिरछा, शीघ्र और हिलता हुआ।
english: On a conjectural reading: with wind (saṃvāta), struck too much (atihata), lifted up (utkṣipta), slanting (tiryak), hurried (druta), shaken (kampita).

text_flags.why: possible: "saṃvāta" is not a standard word in this sense; "with wind" is a guess

notes: A list of ways of administering that end in unit 51 with "doṣāḥ ... praṇetṝṇām". GROUPING: the sentence runs on into unit 51. No noun is stated for the adjectives. Reviewer: saṃvṛta ('covered') is an equally possible reading of the damaged first member; 'with wind' and the suggestion savāta are guesses and should not be relied on.

words.gloss: of those who administer (conjectural reading of the printed form)

hindi: बहुत मन्द, बाहरी, बहुत वेग वाला: ये दोष हैं, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार देने वालों के।
english: Too slow (atimandaka), outer (bāhya), too forceful (ativega): these are faults, on a conjectural reading of those who administer.

text_flags.why: possible: the printed word is not a word; "praṇetṝṇām" (of the administerers) fits the sense

notes: GROUPING: appears to complete unit 50. The sense of "bāhya" is "outer"; unit 68 shows "bāhya" returning quickly, but the text does not explain it. "atimandaka" is read as ati-manda with the suffix -ka.

words.gram: ppp. √dā, loc. sg. (or 3 sg. pres. mid. √dā)

hindi: उच्छ्वास न होने के अनुबन्ध यानी बने रहने में, या दिए जाने पर, या पूरा निःशेष होने पर।
english: In the continuation of non-exhalation (anucchvāsa), or when [it] is given, or [when it] is completely without remainder (niḥśeṣa).
notes: The sense is uncertain: "anucchvāsa" is taken literally as "non-breathing-out" and could refer to air not escaping; "datte niḥśeṣa eva vā" may mean "given with nothing remaining". No subject or noun is stated. GROUPING: the sentence continues in unit 53 ("having entered, the agitated wind ...").
lines_deva: अनुच्छ्वासानुबंधे वा दत्ते निःशेष एव वा
lines_iast: anucchvāsānubaṃdhe vā datte niḥśeṣa eva vā

hindi: प्रवेश करके क्षुब्ध हुई वायु शूल और तोद, यानी चुभन की पीड़ा, करने वाली हो सकती है।
english: The agitated wind (vāyu), having entered, would become a producer of pain (śūla) and pricking pain (toda).
notes: GROUPING: the result of the situations of unit 52. "vāyu" is wind; the text does not say it is the Vāta of the three humours.

words.gloss: sweating, fomentation (conjectural reading of the printed form)

hindi: वहाँ गुदा में अभ्यंग, एक अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार स्वेद, और वात को नष्ट करने वाले भोजन।
english: Here: oil massage (abhyaṅga) on the anus, sweating (sveda, on a conjectural reading of the printed snedo), and Vāta-destroying foods.

text_flags.why: possible: "snedaḥ" is not a word; "svedaḥ" (sweating) fits, as in unit 57; "snehaḥ" (oil) is also possible

notes: Remedy for the pain (śūla) and pricking pain of unit 53. No verb is stated.

hindi: जल्दी डालने पर, बाहर खींचने पर, या अचानक ऊपर उठाने पर भी।
english: When [it] is introduced quickly, or drawn out, or else lifted up suddenly.
notes: The subject (the nozzle or the apparatus) is not stated. The results follow in unit 56. GROUPING: the sentence continues in unit 56.
lines_deva: द्रुतं प्रणीते निष्कृष्टे सहसोत्क्षिप्त एव वा
lines_iast: drutaṃ praṇīte niṣkṛṣṭe sahasotkṣipta eva vā

words.gloss: waist; anus; calf, shank; thigh; bladder (basti); stiffness; very much; splitting pain

hindi: कमर, गुदा, पिंडलियों, जाँघों और बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय में जकड़न और अत्यधिक भेदन यानी फटने की पीड़ा हो सकती है।
english: There would be stiffness (stambha) and severe splitting pain (bhedana) of the waist, anus, calves, thighs and bladder (basti).
notes: The compound could also be read with "ati" going with stambha as well. "basti" is taken here as the bladder, a body site (standard), not the enema bag.

hindi: वहाँ वात को नष्ट करने वाला भोजन, स्वेद, अभ्यंग, बस्तियों यानी एनिमा सहित।
english: Here: Vāta-destroying food, sweating (sveda) and oil massages (abhyaṅga), together with bastis (enemas).
notes: Remedy for the situation of unit 56. No verb is stated. "sabastayaḥ" = "with bastis"; basti here is the enema procedure.

hindi: जब द्वार तिरछी वलि यानी सिलवट से ढका हो, या बँधा हुआ भी हो, तब वह नहीं जाता।
english: When the opening is covered by a slanting fold (valī), or even bound (baddha), it does not go.
notes: The subject of "na gacchati" is not stated (probably the nozzle or the matter administered). "netre" at the start of unit 59 may belong to this sentence. "valī" here is a fold (of skin or mucosa); not further specified.
lines_deva: तिर्यग्वल्यावृतद्वारे बद्धे वा ऽपि न गच्छति

hindi: नेत्र में, उसे सीधा करके बाहर निकालकर और शुद्ध करके फिर से ले जाना चाहिए।
english: In the nozzle: having drawn that out straight and having cleansed [it], one should lead [it] again.
notes: The grammar is loose: "netre" (locative) and "tat" (that) may refer to the same nozzle. "punar nayet" is rendered literally "should lead again". GROUPING: remedy for the situation of unit 58.
lines_deva: नेत्रे तदृजु निष्कास्य संशोध्य च पुनर्नयेत्
lines_iast: netre tadṛju niṣkāsya saṃśodhya ca punarnayet

hindi: दबाए जाते समय बीच में छोड़ देने पर, गुदा में वायु रुकी हुई, टकराकर लौटी हुई।
english: When [it] is being pressed and is let go in between, in the anus the wind (anila), obstructed (pratihata) ...

text_flags.why: possible: extra ṃ in the print

notes: GROUPING: the sentence continues in unit 61 ("... the strong one would produce pain in the chest and head"). The subject of "pīḍyamāne" and "mukte" is not stated.

hindi: छाती और सिर में पीड़ा, और जाँघों में अवसाद यानी शिथिलता, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, बलवान उत्पन्न कर सकता है।
english: The strong one (balī, on a conjectural reading of the printed valī) would produce pain in the chest and head, and sinking (sāda, exhaustion) of the thighs.

text_flags.why: possible: "valī" is a fold (as in unit 58) and does not fit a subject; "balī" (strong, i.e. the wind of unit 60) fits

notes: GROUPING: appears to complete unit 60; the subject is probably the wind (anila) of unit 60, but the text does not say so. v/b spellings are interchangeable in this print.

words.gloss: bilva (wood-apple, Aegle marmelos; standard) and the rest; fruit; śyāmā (disputed: often trivṛt, turpeth, Operculina turpethum in Āyurvedic usage, other plants also proposed) and the rest; urine; possessing

hindi: वहाँ बस्ति यानी एनिमा बिल्व यानी बेल आदि, फल, श्यामा आदि और मूत्र वाली हो।
english: There the basti (enema) should be one with bilva (wood-apple) and the rest, fruit, śyāmā and the rest, and urine.
notes: Identifications: bilva = Aegle marmelos, wood-apple (standard); śyāmā = disputed (commonly read as trivṛt, turpeth; other plants also proposed), not carried into the translation; whether "bilvādi" and "śyāmādi" are named groups, and what "phala" (fruit) is, are not stated; the kind of urine is not stated. The compound can also be read as "bilvādi-phala" (fruits of the bilva group).

hindi: दाह, दवथु यानी तपन, शोफ यानी सूजन, कम्पन: गुदा के आहत होने पर।
english: There would be burning (dāha), burning distress (davathu), swelling (śopha) and trembling (kampana), when the anus is injured.
notes: "kampanābhihate" is read as kampana + abhihate. It could also be one compound "struck by trembling", which seems less likely.

hindi: वहाँ कसैले और मीठे, ठंडे सेक यानी धार डालना, बस्तियों यानी एनिमा सहित।
english: Here: astringent and sweet, cool affusions (seka), together with bastis (enemas).
notes: "kaṣāya" is taken as the taste (astringent) because it stands beside madhura (sweet); it could also mean a decoction. Remedy for the burning and swelling of unit 63.

hindi: मात्रा से अधिक डाली गई नली से, वलि के क्षत होने से।
english: By a nozzle introduced beyond measure (atimātra), from the wounding of the fold (bali),
notes: GROUPING: the sentence continues in unit 66. "bali" is a fold (the anal folds are probably meant, not stated). "atimātra" = beyond the proper measure of insertion.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार पीड़ा, दाह, चुभन की पीड़ा, और भारी मल का निकलना होगा।
english: On a conjectural reading there would be pain, burning (dāha), pricking pain (nistoda), and the passing of heavy stool.

text_flags.why: possible: "sarti" is not a word; "ārti" (pain) is a guess; "sṛti" (flow) is also possible

notes: Result of unit 65. The first member after syāt is unclear and rendered by a guess; the other members are clear. "guruvarcas" = heavy stool.

words.gloss: unclear (printed form; probably picchā, a slimy substance)

hindi: वहाँ घी, पिच्छु, दूध और पिच्छा-बस्ति यानी पिच्छा नामक लसलसे पदार्थ की एनिमा, प्रशस्त हैं।
english: There ghee (sarpis), picchu (unclear; on a conjectural reading a slimy substance), milk, and the picchā-basti (enema) are recommended.

text_flags.why: possible: "picchu" is not a known word; "picchā" (slime) fits "picchābasti"

notes: Remedy for the situation of unit 66. The singular verb śasyate serves a list. The kind of picchā is not stated. Reviewer (probable, not stated in the text): picchā in picchā-basti is, in Ayurvedic usage, the sticky gum of the śālmali (silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba); the Sanskrit here only says picchā-basti.

hindi: मन्द भावित नहीं करता, और बाहरी शीघ्र लौट आता है।
english: The slow (one) does not impregnate (bhāvayati), and the outer (one) returns quickly.
notes: No noun is stated for "slow" and "outer" (they presumably refer to the faults of 51); none is supplied. "bhāvayati" has no object stated.

hindi: वहाँ स्नेह यानी चिकना द्रव्य फिर ठीक से देना चाहिए, सफलता चाहने वाले को।
english: There an unctuous substance (sneha) should be administered again properly, by one who wishes for success (siddhi).
notes: Remedy for the situation of unit 68. "sneha" is an unctuous substance (oil or fat); the kind is not stated.

hindi: बहुत दबाया हुआ, कोष्ठ यानी पेट में ठहरता है, या गले तक आ जाता है।
english: Pressed too much, [it] stays in the koṣṭha (belly) or comes to the throat.
notes: The subject is not stated. The remedy follows in unit 71. "koṣṭha" = storehouse, belly.

words.gloss: throat; pressing; and so on; procedure

hindi: वहाँ बस्ति यानी एनिमा, विरेक यानी दस्त लाना, और गले को दबाने से आरम्भ होने वाला कर्म।
english: There: basti (enema), purgation (vireka), and the procedure (karma) beginning with pressing of the throat (galapīḍā).
notes: "galapīḍā" can mean pressing of the throat or pain of the throat; the first is taken, in line with unit 32 (kaṇṭhagraha). No verb is stated. GROUPING: remedy for unit 70.

hindi: वमन आदि से शुद्ध किया हुआ, और कृश देह, बल और अनल वाला।
english: Purified by emesis (vamana) and the rest, and with emaciated body, strength and fire (anala).
notes: GROUPING: the sentence runs on to unit 74, where the physician is the subject. No noun is stated for the patient. "kṣāma" may qualify only deha, or all three; left open. "anala" = fire, not specified further. Reviewer (probable): anala here, beside bala, most likely means the digestive fire; the Sanskrit says only 'fire'.

hindi: जैसे कोमल अंडा, जैसे तेल से भरा पात्र, वैसे।
english: As a tender egg, as a vessel full of oil, so ...
notes: GROUPING: the comparison continues in unit 74. No verb is stated.
